Before anything else, read **Proposing a broker** and **Capture first, then
write** in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md). They are short, and they
are what a manifest is judged against.

The three things that decide whether this goes anywhere:

**The site's own opt-out page.** The address, reached from that site. A broker
enters through its own page and no other door: seeing one named in an
advertisement, linked from another broker's results, or listed on a roundup
is a lead, not a source.

**What the page asks for.** A name? An email address? A listing URL? A
document? Does anything have to be confirmed by email or by phone? Does it
say how long removal takes, and in whose words?

**What stands in the way.** A CAPTCHA, a terms dialog, a bot check, an
account requirement, a payment. Say which, because that decides whether a
manifest can describe the flow at all or whether it stops and hands over.

You do not have to write the manifest. A proposal with a real opt-out address
and an honest description of what the page asks is useful on its own, and
somebody else can do the capture.

If you do want to write it: capture the page and commit the image first, then
write the manifest from that image in a second commit. Every selector's label
has to be legible on a capture, and every claim the manifest makes about what
the page says has to be readable there too. Crop to the claims rather than to
a tidy frame.

**No real person's data anywhere**, in the issue or in a pull request: no
name, address, phone number, email address, date of birth, verification code,
or one-time link. That includes yours.
